content.title: About
content.content: Boneless, skinless chicken breast is a lean source of high‑quality protein. Raw breast meat is light pink, tender, and has a neutral flavor that readily absorbs seasonings during cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast contains less fat than most other parts of the bird.
One hundred grams of raw breast provides about 31 g of protein, making it one of the most protein‑dense foods.
Chicken was domesticated over 8,000 years ago in Southeast Asia.
Because it has little connective tissue, breast cooks quickly and stays juicy when prepared properly.
Raw chicken breast is often used in marinades and sushi‑style dishes where freshness is key.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Protein is essential for muscle growth, tissue repair, and enzyme production.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The low saturated‑fat content makes breast suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6) support energy metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports immune function.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Chicken provides phosphorus and small amounts of calcium, both important for bone tissue.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; keep it at ≤ 4 °C and cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C.

items.title: Bird‑meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals can develop allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: High sodium in processed versions
items.content: Pre‑marinated breasts can contain added salt, which should be considered in sodium‑restricted diets.

items.title: Spoilage if stored improperly
items.content: When kept longer than 2 days in the fridge, the meat may spoil; check for off‑odors and discoloration.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken breast can be grilled, baked, boiled, steamed, or added to salads. A simple marinade of olive oil, lemon juice, herbs, and spices works well. Diced breast is used in sushi rolls, stir‑fries, and quick‑cook meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a low‑air‑permeable bag at –18 °C for up to 9 months. Thaw frozen breast in the refrigerator before use.
